title: 3.3 A Passive Switched-Capacitor-Based Multimode Amplifier with a Logarithmic Conformity Error of 0.75% from -25 to 200°C
problem: Harsh geothermal and high-temperature environments (up to 200°C) require sensor front-end amplifiers with wide dynamic range (>80dB), low temperature drift, and accurate phase/amplitude across extreme temperature spans. Existing logarithmic amplifiers exhibit high temperature dependence; low-drift amplifiers require complex trimming and compensation.
motivation: Renewable energy applications (geothermal) and harsh-environment IoT require integrated electronics that maintain signal integrity across extreme temperature swings, but traditional amplifier designs fail or require extensive trimming.
method: A passive switched-capacitor (SC) topology with multimode operation achieves high dynamic range and temperature stability. The design leverages discrete-time SC amplification to improve noise efficiency while avoiding the thermal drift issues of traditional logarithmic or low-drift amplifiers, using novel compensation mechanisms for stability across -25 to 200°C.
key_novelty: Passive switched-capacitor multimode amplifier achieving 0.75% logarithmic conformity error across -25 to 200°C without requiring trimmed ratios or complex temperature compensation circuits.
contributions: Logarithmic conformity error of 0.75% over extreme temperature range (-25 to 200°C)
Wide dynamic range >80dB maintained across temperature extremes
Passive SC topology eliminating complex trimming and temperature compensation overhead
Improved reliability for high-temperature geothermal and sensor applications
primary_theme: High-temperature sensor amplification via passive switched-capacitor topology
